description: Theoretical performance estimates and web-search references for GPU compute workloads. Used by estimate_performance() and search_benchmarks() tools.

hardware_theoretical.description: Theoretical peak performance per architecture for common LLM workloads. Derived from vendor specs (CU count × clock × ops/cycle).
hardware_theoretical.notes: Real-world performance is 10-50% of theoretical due to memory bandwidth limits. Use as a ceiling estimate, not a target.

gfx1030.name: RDNA2 (RX 6900 XT class)
known_bottlenecks: No WMMA/rocWMMA → attention uses slow F32 path
Older dot4 (v_dot4_i32_i8) ~30% slower than RDNA3 packed dot4
LDS only 64KiB → shared memory limited

gfx1201.name: RDNA4 (RX 9070 XT class)
known_bottlenecks: No WMMA — same F32 fallback as gfx1030 for attention
128KiB LDS — can use larger shared memory tiles
17% higher memory bandwidth vs gfx1100

sm_89.name: Ada Lovelace (RTX 4090 class)
known_bottlenecks: FP8 mixed precision requires careful scaling
Transformer engine auto-mixed-precision tuning needed for peak perf

sm_90.name: Hopper (H100-class)
known_bottlenecks: FP8 requires dynamic loss scaling (Transformer Engine)
MHA/MQSA/GQA kernels require custom Triton/Hopper implementations
High memory bandwidth makes dequant less of a bottleneck

gfx90a.name: CDNA2 (MI200/MI250X)
known_bottlenecks: CDNA2 rocWMMA uses different intrinsics than RDNA (v_wmma_* vs __builtin_amdgcn_*_gcn)
CDNA1/CDNA2 matrix core instructions differ — separate code paths needed

gfx1105.name: RDNA3 APU (Phoenix/Raphael-R)
known_bottlenecks: No WMMA/rocWMMA — attention uses F32 fallback
Limited memory bandwidth (72 GB/s) makes memory-bound kernels 5-10× slower than discrete
8 compute units → low parallelism for large batch sizes
DP4a recommended for integer matmul (GL_KHR_shader_integer_dot_product via Vulkan)

meteor_lake.name: Intel Core Ultra 5 135H iGPU
known_bottlenecks: Integrated GPU shares DDR5 memory — 72 GB/s vs 960 GB/s for discrete
Power envelope (28W) throttles under sustained load
No dedicated VRAM → cache misses are expensive
Vulkan CM support requires Mesa 24.3+ — check `kands://isa-references`

strix_point.name: AMD Strix Point APU (Ryzen AI 9 365, RDNA 3 iGPU gfx1100-class, 12 CU)
known_bottlenecks: 12 CU RDNA 3 iGPU — low parallelism vs discrete (96 CU on RX 7900 XTX)
Shared DDR5/LPDDR5X memory — 72 GB/s bandwidth bottleneck
Laptop power/thermal constrained — sustained perf limited
WMMA available on gfx1100 iGPU — use WMMA path for fp16 matmul
Best for 7B-13B Q4_0/Q5_1 models on laptop

strix_halos.name: AMD Strix Halo APU (Radeon 8060S, RDNA 3.5 iGPU gfx1150-class, 40 CU rumored)
known_bottlenecks: 40 CU RDNA 3.5 iGPU — much better than Strix Point (12 CU), but still far below discrete (96 CU on RX 7900 XTX)
Shared DDR5/LPDDR5X memory — 128 GB/s bandwidth (better than Strix Point's 72 GB/s, still far below discrete 960 GB/s)
Laptop power/thermal constrained — sustained perf limited vs desktop
WMMA available on gfx1150 iGPU — use WMMA path for fp16 matmul
Best for 13B-30B Q4_0/Q5_1 models on laptop (more CU + more memory BW than Strix Point)
Status: rumored/upcoming — verify exact CU count and feature set when hardware ships

zen3.name: AMD Zen 3 (Ryzen 5000 series, Vermeer, CPU-only, no iGPU compute target)

workload_estimates.fp32_gemm_4096_cpu: 1.7 GFLOPS (AVX2 + FMA3, 2 FMA/cycle × 12 cores × 2 threads × 4 FLOP/FMA × 3.4GHz ≈ 1.8 GFLOPS theoretical)
workload_estimates.fp16_gemm_4096_cpu: 1.7 GFLOPS (AVX2 fp16 packed — no native fp16, emulated via f16c)
workload_estimates.bf16_gemm_4096_cpu: 1.7 GFLOPS (emulated via AVX2 — no native BF16 on Zen 3)
workload_estimates.int8_dequant: 12 cores × 3.4GHz × 16 int8 ops/cycle (AVX2 vpmaddwd) ≈ 653 GOPS theoretical, ~500 GOPS practical
workload_estimates.flash_attn_4096_cpu: N/A — CPU attention for LLM is not practical; use GPU offload

known_bottlenecks: No AVX-512 (AMD dropped it on Zen 2/Zen 3) — if CPU kernel uses AVX-512, rewrite for AVX2
No AMX (AMX is Zen 4+) — no hardware matrix extension for GEMM
No native BF16 (BF16 on Zen 3 is emulated via AVX2 — slower than native)
No native FP16 (FP16 on Zen 3 is emulated via F16C instruction — has FP16 conversion but not FP16 math)
12 cores × 2 threads = 24 threads — enough for parallel CPU inference but not competitive with GPU
Memory bandwidth 51 GB/s (DDR4-3200 dual-channel) — far below GPU memory BW
zen3.best_for: CPU host for HIP/ROCm builds (hipcc uses Clang, CPU ISA fine), CPU kernel path (AVX2 + FMA3 fallback), CUDA host on Linux (GCC 11+ / Clang 12+)
zen3.not_for: GPU compute (no iGPU on Zen 3 desktop), any GPU-accelerated LLM inference, AVX-512-dependent CPU kernels, AMX-dependent CPU kernels

workload_estimates.avx512_gemm_4096_cpu: 3.0 GFLOPS (AVX-512 + FMA3, 2 FMA/cycle × 10 cores × 2 threads × 8 FLOP/FMA × 3.5GHz ≈ 3.2 GFLOPS theoretical — but 10th Gen AVX-512 is slower due to 14nm thermal limits)
workload_estimates.fp16_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.0 GFLOPS (AVX2 fp16 packed — no native fp16, emulated via f16c)
workload_estimates.bf16_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.0 GFLOPS (emulated via AVX2 — no native BF16 on 10th Gen Intel)
workload_estimates.int8_dequant: 10 cores × 3.5GHz × 16 int8 ops/cycle (AVX2) ≈ 560 GOPS theoretical, ~450 GOPS practical
workload_estimates.flash_attn_4096_cpu: N/A — CPU attention for LLM is not practical; use GPU offload

known_bottlenecks: 10nm+14nm hybrid not applicable (10th Gen is 14nm only, no hybrid)
AVX-512 available but thermal-limited (14nm, 140W+ TDP on i9-10900K)
No AMX (AMX is 12th Gen+) — no hardware matrix extension for GEMM
No native BF16 (BF16 on Intel 10th Gen is emulated via AVX2 — slower than native)
No native FP16 (FP16 on Intel 10th Gen is emulated via F16C)
10 cores × 2 threads = 20 threads — enough for parallel CPU inference but not competitive with GPU
Memory bandwidth 51 GB/s (DDR4-3200 dual-channel) — far below GPU memory BW
iGPU is Gen12 LP UHD (1-2 CU) — NOT a compute target (no DPAS, no WMMA)
intel_10th.best_for: CPU host for CUDA builds on Windows (MSVC 2019 v142), CPU host for oneAPI builds on Linux (GCC 10+), CPU kernel path (AVX2 + AVX-512 available)
intel_10th.not_for: GPU compute (iGPU is not a compute target), any GPU-accelerated LLM inference, AMX-dependent CPU kernels

intel_12th.name: Intel 12th Gen (Alder Lake, 10nm + 14nm hybrid, CPU-only, no iGPU compute target)

workload_estimates.fp32_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.0 GFLOPS (AVX2 + FMA3, 2 FMA/cycle × 8 P-cores × 2 threads × 4 FLOP/FMA × 3.6GHz ≈ 2.1 GFLOPS theoretical from P-cores only; E-cores don't add much)
workload_estimates.fp16_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.0 GFLOPS (AVX2 fp16 packed — no native fp16, emulated via f16c)
workload_estimates.bf16_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.0 GFLOPS (emulated via AVX2 — no native BF16 on 12th Gen Intel)
workload_estimates.int8_dequant: 8 P-cores × 3.6GHz × 16 int8 ops/cycle (AVX2) ≈ 461 GOPS theoretical, ~370 GOPS practical (P-cores only; E-cores add some but lower IPC)
workload_estimates.flash_attn_4096_cpu: N/A — CPU attention for LLM is not practical; use GPU offload

known_bottlenecks: Hybrid P-core + E-core — AVX-512 DISABLED (Intel disabled AVX-512 on all hybrid arch)

No AMX (AMX is 12th Gen+ but only on some SKUs — 12th Gen Alder Lake has AMX on P-cores? Check: AMX is available on 12th Gen Intel Xeon and some Core SKUs, but Alder Lake consumer i9-12900K has AMX. However AMX is for server/workstation, not consumer. On 12th Gen Core i9-12900K, AMX is NOT available — AMX came to consumer with Meteor Lake? Actually AMX is on Sapphire Rapids (Xeon) first, then some Core SKUs. 12th Gen Core i9-12900K does NOT have AMX. AMX on consumer Intel starts with... actually AMX is not on any consumer Intel CPU as of 14th Gen. AMX is Xeon-only.)

intel_12th.not_for: GPU compute (iGPU is not a compute target unless SKU has Arc graphics), any GPU-accelerated LLM inference, AVX-512-dependent CPU kernels (AVX-512 is gone on 12th Gen+)

workload_estimates.fp32_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.2 GFLOPS (AVX2 + FMA3, 2 FMA/cycle × 8 P-cores × 2 threads × 4 FLOP/FMA × 3.7GHz ≈ 2.2 GFLOPS theoretical from P-cores only; E-cores add some but lower IPC)
workload_estimates.fp16_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.2 GFLOPS (AVX2 fp16 packed — no native fp16, emulated via f16c)
workload_estimates.bf16_gemm_4096_cpu: 2.2 GFLOPS (emulated via AVX2 — no native BF16 on 13th Gen Intel)
workload_estimates.int8_dequant: 8 P-cores × 3.7GHz × 16 int8 ops/cycle (AVX2) ≈ 474 GOPS theoretical, ~380 GOPS practical (P-cores only)
workload_estimates.flash_attn_4096_cpu: N/A — CPU attention for LLM is not practical; use GPU offload

known_bottlenecks: Hybrid P-core + E-core — AVX-512 DISABLED (same as 12th Gen — Intel disabled AVX-512 on all hybrid arch)
No AMX (AMX is Xeon-only — not on consumer 13th Gen Core i9-13900K)
No native BF16 (BF16 on Intel 13th Gen is emulated via AVX2 — slower than native)
No native FP16 (FP16 on Intel 13th Gen is emulated via F16C)
